title: SDK Parity Matrix v1 (Python / TypeScript / Go) — Auth, Retries, Timeouts, Streaming, Errors
content:
Working doc (v1) — sheet-style parity matrix for Redwood Hosted API SDKs.

Purpose
- Capture current client behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go for auth, retries, timeouts, streaming, and errors.
- Highlight gaps driving support load + enterprise review friction.
- Propose target behavior for the “SDK Client Behavior Standard” (to be moved into Confluence + ADRs).

Scope notes
- In scope: Hosted API SDKs (py/ts/go), including streaming endpoints; retry + timeout defaults; error taxonomy; auth config; optional telemetry hooks.
- Out of scope: server-side gateway retry policies; major API surface redesign.

Legend
- “Current” = observed in latest released SDKs as of 2025-01-13 (best effort; please correct).
- “Target” = proposed vNext default for parity; may be revised after SRE/Security/Platform review.
- “Deviation acceptable?” = if we intentionally keep differences (try to minimize).

Table columns
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking

---
AUTHENTICATION
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Auth | Env var name(s) supported | REDWOOD_API_KEY (confirmed); also accepts REDWOOD_KEY? (unclear) | REDWOOD_API_KEY; also supports REDWOOD_TOKEN in older examples | REDWOOD_API_KEY only | Env var ambiguity causes enterprise review + support confusion (SUP-9355) | Single env var: REDWOOD_API_KEY only. Deprecate others with warning in docs | Pending Security sign-off | Marcus Lin / Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2484
Auth | Header name used | Sends Authorization: Bearer <key> | Sends Authorization: Bearer <key> (some examples show X-API-Key) | Uses X-API-Key by default (older) | Header mismatch breaks gateway expectations + inconsistent customer configs | Standardize to Authorization: Bearer <key> for all SDKs. Accept X-API-Key only as opt-in override for legacy | Pending Platform/Gateway confirmation | Ethan Park / Amara Diallo | ENG-2484
Auth | Config precedence order | Constructor arg > env var > config file (only env var implemented today) | Constructor arg > env var | Constructor arg > env var | Lack of consistent precedence complicates multi-tenant apps | Standard precedence: explicit per-client option > env var > (optional) shared config file (phase 2). No implicit keychain reads | Draft proposal | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2484
Auth | Support reading keys from local files | No | No | No | Security thread asked “should we read from files?”; risk of secret sprawl | Default: NO file reads. If we add, it must be explicit path + documented as advanced; never by default | Pending Security | Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei | ENG-2484
Auth | Error when key missing | Raises generic ValueError; message: “api_key required” | Throws Error; message varies by runtime (sometimes “Missing API Key”) | Returns error; message “missing api key” but no remediation | Support asks for “do X, set Y env var” guidance (SUP-9355) | Standard message template across SDKs: “Missing API key. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass apiKey in client options.” (no key echo) | Draft | Elliot Price (messaging) / SDK leads | ENG-2489
Auth | Redaction in logs/exceptions | Partial: some debug logs include headers if debug enabled | Risk: some customers log full request init object | Go debug logs include headers in trace mode | Security requires redaction; enterprise reviews flag it | Never log Authorization header; redact if user logs raw request object via hooks (provide safe hooks). Ensure exceptions never include key value | Pending Security | Marcus Lin / Dana Lo / Mateusz Zielinski | ENG-2484
Auth | Multi-tenant: per-request override | Possible by instantiating multiple clients; no per-request auth override | Some internal helper allows per-request headers | Context-based request options allow per-request headers | Multi-tenant SaaS wants per-request key without building client pools | Provide per-request override as an explicit escape hatch: requestOptions.headers.authorization. Must be opt-in and clearly documented as advanced | Draft | Brian Murphy / SDK leads | ENG-2484
Auth | Header casing normalization | Python uses requests/httpx normalized | TS depends on fetch/undici; casing not guaranteed | Go canonicalizes headers | Some gateways/proxies case-insensitive but customers copy/paste raw logs | No requirement; ensure behavior doesn’t break; tests should treat headers case-insensitive | Acceptable deviation | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2485

---
RETRIES
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Retries | Default retries enabled? | Enabled in some methods (inconsistent); streaming: off | Enabled by default; aggressive on 429 in some cases | Mostly no retries by default (except transport) | TS retry storms on 429 (SUP-9334); Python inconsistency triggers “why did it retry?” tickets | Retries ON by default for safe operations with strict budgets + jitter. Streaming: default NO auto-resume (see streaming section) | Under review w/ SRE | Rafael Mendes / Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2482
Retries | Retryable status codes | 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 (varies by endpoint) | 429 + many 5xx; sometimes retries 408 | 502/503/504 only | Inconsistent reliability; some clients never recover from flaps | Retryable: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. Do NOT retry 400/401/403/404/422. 408/409 only if explicitly opted-in (rare) | Draft | Ibrahim Khan / Dana Lo / Mateusz Zielinski | ENG-2482
Retries | Retryable transport errors | Connect reset, DNS, socket timeout: partial | Depends on runtime; undici fetch throws TypeError; classifier too broad | net.Error timeout + temporary: partial | Unpredictable (TS retries on non-transient fetch errors) | Standard classifier: retry network connect errors, TLS handshake failures (transient), connection reset, EOF before response headers. Do not retry after partial body unless idempotent + safe | Needs spec detail | SRE + SDK leads | ENG-2482
Retries | Max attempts default | 5 (some methods 3) | 6 | 2 | Too many attempts amplifies throttling; too few reduces reliability | Default max attempts = 3 total attempts (1 initial + 2 retries) for non-streaming. For 429 specifically: allow up to 4 total if Retry-After present and budget allows | Under review | Rafael Mendes | ENG-2482
Retries | Backoff strategy | Exponential backoff; jitter inconsistent | Exponential; jitter minimal (low entropy) | Linear-ish with cap | Risk of thundering herd; SRE asked for full jitter | Exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (or full jitter) + cap. Suggested: base=250ms, cap=4s. Respect Retry-After for 429/503 when provided | Draft | Rafael Mendes / Dana Lo | ENG-2482
Retries | Respect Retry-After header | Partial | Sometimes ignored | Ignored | Gateway provides Retry-After; ignoring prolongs throttling | Must respect Retry-After (seconds/date). If Retry-After > 10s, surface error unless user opts-in to long waits | Pending gateway header guarantees | Amara Diallo / Ethan Park | ENG-2482
Retries | Per-request override | Some support via request options (not uniform) | Supported | Limited | Enterprise wants ability to disable retries for some calls | Expose standard options: maxAttempts, retryEnabled, retryOn (list), maxRetryDelayMs. Per-request overrides must not exceed global retry budget | Draft | Brian Murphy | ENG-2482
Retries | Retry budget (time) | None | None | None | Retry storms during partial outages | Add retry budget (elapsed time) default 10s non-streaming; stop retrying when exceeded even if attempts remain | Under review | Rafael Mendes | ENG-2482
Retries | Idempotency interaction | No idempotency key support in SDK | No idempotency key support | No idempotency key support | Risk: retrying POST may duplicate side effects (future endpoints) | For current Hosted API inference calls: treat as safe to retry pre-response. When idempotency keys introduced, SDK should auto-add for non-streaming POSTs (future) | Note / non-goal for this phase | Ethan Park / Brian Murphy | API standards doc TBD
Retries | Telemetry hooks on retry | No standardized hooks | Some internal callback | None | Hard to debug “why did it retry” | Add optional hooks: onRetry(attempt, delayMs, reason, requestId?) without exposing secrets; emit counters for attempts and final outcome | Draft | Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman | ENG-2490
Retries | Retry on 429 when rate-limited by token bucket | TS retries quickly; worsens throttle | TS is main offender | Go doesn’t retry enough | Support case: extended throttling from aggressive retries (SUP-9334) | 429 handling: always respect Retry-After; if absent, use backoff + treat as “hard” throttle after 1-2 retries (surface quickly) | Under review | Rafael Mendes / Dana Lo | ENG-2482
Retries | Retry on 500 with JSON error body | Python sometimes surfaces immediately if body parsed | TS retries | Go surfaces | Platform intermittent 500s; desire consistent | Retry regardless of body presence as long as response not streamed and request not partially consumed | Draft | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2482

---
TIMEOUTS
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Timeouts | Default overall timeout (non-streaming) | 60s (httpx default overridden?) | No default (infinite) in Node fetch; some examples set 30s | 30s via http.Client Timeout | “Hanging” calls in TS; inconsistent customer behavior | Standard default overall timeout: 60s for non-streaming generation; 30s for embeddings; configurable per request | Draft | Ibrahim Khan / Dana Lo / Mateusz Zielinski | ENG-2489
Timeouts | Connect timeout | 5s | Not explicit (depends on runtime) | Dial timeout 10s (default transport) | Proxy/network issues cause long hangs | Default connect timeout: 5s across SDKs (where supported). In TS implement via AbortController timer if runtime lacks connect separate | Needs implementation detail | Dana Lo | ENG-2487
Timeouts | Read/inactivity timeout for streaming | Python: none (can “hang” on proxy buffering) | TS: none; relies on user abort | Go: none | SUP-9321: python streaming appears hung then errors; proxies buffer SSE | Default streaming inactivity timeout: 60s w/ reset on each SSE event. If no bytes/events for 60s, abort with TimeoutError and suggest proxy config | Under review | Ibrahim Khan / Mateusz Zielinski | ENG-2483
Timeouts | Timeout error type mapping | Raises httpx.ReadTimeout sometimes; custom TimeoutError elsewhere | Throws AbortError/DOMException/TypeError depending | context deadline exceeded vs net.Error timeout | Customers can’t write portable error handling | Normalize to SDK-level TimeoutError with fields: kind=connect|read|overall; isTimeout=true; preserve underlying error as cause | Draft | SDK leads | ENG-2489
Timeouts | Distinguish timeout vs user cancel | Python conflates cancel exceptions sometimes | TS abort treated as error but message unclear | Go context cancel vs deadline inconsistent (SUP-9342) | Support + customer code needs to know if user cancelled | Provide CancellationError distinct from TimeoutError. In Go: map context.Canceled to CancellationError; context.DeadlineExceeded to TimeoutError | Draft | Mateusz Zielinski | ENG-2488
Timeouts | Per-request override UX | client.timeout = X | requestOptions.timeoutMs exists in some methods | context with deadline on caller | Hard to find consistent setting | Standard per-request option name: timeoutMs (overall) and streamingInactivityTimeoutMs. In Go keep context as primary but also allow options for convenience | Draft | Brian Murphy | ENG-2489
Timeouts | Document recommended timeouts | Minimal | Minimal | Minimal | Customers set too low and blame SDK | Add docs table: suggested defaults by endpoint + production guidance (esp. streaming) | Planned | Elliot Price / Wei Chen | ENG-2491

---
STREAMING (SSE)
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Streaming | SSE framing parsing robustness | Python fails on partial frames in some proxies | TS sometimes drops last chunk on disconnect | Go reader splits lines; partial reads can corrupt event parsing | Slack thread: partial SSE frames + proxies | Harden SSE parser: tolerate partial lines, CRLF/LF, trailing spaces. Only emit events when full “\n\n” frame complete | Draft | Dana Lo / Mateusz Zielinski | ENG-2483
Streaming | Event types supported | data only | data + event? inconsistent | data only | Inconsistent; docs unclear | Standardize: accept “event:” and “data:” lines; emit typed events: message, error, done. Ignore unknown fields | Draft | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2483
Streaming | DONE sentinel handling | Python: [DONE] literal | TS: uses “done” event | Go: [DONE] | Customers see different final chunks | Standard: treat [DONE] as end-of-stream marker for compatibility; SDK should NOT surface [DONE] as a token; instead close iterator/stream gracefully | Draft | SDK leads | ENG-2483
Streaming | Mid-stream disconnect behavior | Python surfaces generic network error | TS sometimes reconnects implicitly via fetch retry wrappers | Go returns EOF | Support escalation: TS streaming disconnect semantics inconsistent | No automatic reconnect/resume by default. If disconnect occurs after any content delivered, surface StreamDisconnectedError with partial output available and requestId if known | Under review | Ibrahim Khan / Dana Lo | ENG-2483
Streaming | Safe retry/resume guidance | None | None | None | Users attempt naive retries; may duplicate tokens | Document: do not retry mid-stream unless application-level idempotency/offset support exists (not present today). Provide pattern: restart whole request with “best effort” semantics, only if acceptable | Draft (docs) | Elliot Price / Sabrina James | ENG-2491
Streaming | Cancellation semantics | Python generator close cancels? not deterministic | TS AbortController cancellation works but error type varies | Go context cancel sometimes returns timeout-ish error | Need consistent cancel across SDKs | Standard: user cancellation should stop reading immediately, close underlying connection, and raise CancellationError (not TimeoutError). Must be deterministic in tests | Draft | Mateusz Zielinski / Dana Lo | ENG-2483
Streaming | Backpressure | Python yields tokens; ok | TS event emitter pushes; possible memory growth | Go scanner buffers; risk | High-volume streams may blow memory | Provide pull-based async iterator/reader as primary interface; if push-based exists, document backpressure and buffer limits | Open question | Dana Lo | ENG-2483
Streaming | Proxy buffering detection | None | None | None | SUP-9321 suggests buffering hides events then large burst | Heuristic: if headers show “text/event-stream” but no data for inactivity timeout, error message should mention proxy buffering + suggest disabling buffering for SSE | Draft | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2483
Streaming | Content-type validation | Not strict | Not strict | Not strict | Debugging hard when server returns HTML error | If status != 200 or content-type not text/event-stream, do not start SSE parser; parse JSON error if possible and raise SDK error with status/body snippet (redacted) | Draft | Brian Murphy | ENG-2483

---
ERROR TAXONOMY + MESSAGES
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Errors | Base error type | Python raises mixed (httpx + SDK) | JS Error only | Go error only | Hard to catch and inspect | Introduce SDK error hierarchy (or interfaces): RedwoodError base; ApiError(status, code, requestId); RateLimitError; TimeoutError; CancellationError; RetryExhaustedError; StreamDisconnectedError | Draft | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2489
Errors | Include request-id in errors | Sometimes present if user inspects headers | Rare | Rare | Support always asks for request-id; customers don’t have it | Always capture response request-id header (if present) and attach to all ApiError types + log hook | Depends on platform header guarantee | Ethan Park / Amara Diallo | ENG-2490
Errors | Include response status/body safely | Python includes full body sometimes | TS includes full response in some error paths | Go includes little detail | Risk of leaking secrets; also too little detail blocks debugging | Standard: include status, error code, request-id, and short message. Include body snippet (max 1KB) only when content-type is JSON and redacted; never include Authorization | Pending Security | Marcus Lin | ENG-2489
Errors | Map 401/403 to auth errors | Mixed | Mixed | Mixed | Customers get generic errors | 401 -> AuthenticationError; 403 -> PermissionDeniedError; include remediation: “check API key, org/project, scopes” | Draft | Ibrahim Khan | ENG-2489
Errors | Rate limit error payload parsing | Python ignores structured fields | TS ignores | Go ignores | Platform working on machine-readable fields | Parse fields if present: retryAfterMs, limit, remaining, reset, policy. If absent, fall back to Retry-After header | Pending platform payload changes | Amara Diallo / SDK leads | ENG-2482
Errors | Retry exhaustion error | Python surfaces last error only | TS surfaces generic error | Go surfaces last error | Customers can’t tell it retried | Raise RetryExhaustedError including attempts, elapsedMs, lastError (as cause), and list of retry reasons (capped) | Draft | Rafael Mendes | ENG-2489
Errors | Consistent messages | Not consistent | Not consistent | Not consistent | Docs/migration hard | Align message templates for top cases (missing key, rate limit, timeout, stream disconnect). Keep concise + actionable | Draft | Elliot Price | ENG-2489

---
REQUEST IDS + DEBUG HOOKS (OBSERVABILITY)
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Obs | Send client request id header | No | No | No | Hard to trace client-side | Optionally generate client-side id (UUIDv4) and send as X-Client-Request-Id (or Redwood-Client-Request-Id) if gateway agrees. Always prefer server request-id in support | Needs gateway standard | Ethan Park / Allison Grant | ENG-2490
Obs | Logging hooks | Ad-hoc | Ad-hoc | Ad-hoc | Customers log secrets accidentally | Provide structured hooks: onRequest, onResponse, onError, onRetry. Default no-op. Provide “safe logger” helper that redacts headers | Draft | Nadia Rahman / Logan Wright | ENG-2490
Obs | Surface rate limit headers | Not consistently exposed | Not exposed | Not exposed | Customers want to self-throttle | Expose parsed rate-limit info on successful responses (optional) and on RateLimitError | Pending platform headers | Amara Diallo | ENG-2490

---
CONFORMANCE TEST HARNESS (for parity gating)
Area | Behavior / requirement | Python (current) | TypeScript (current) | Go (current) | Gap / risk / support signal | Proposed target behavior (cross-SDK) | Decision status | Owner | Tracking
Conformance | Mock gateway scenarios exist | No | No | No | Parity regresses release-over-release | Build shared scenario spec + per-language adapters. Scenarios: 429 burst with Retry-After, 503 flap, connect reset, streaming partial frame, mid-stream disconnect, timeout vs cancel | Planned | Sahana Iyer / Leila Farouk | ENG-2485
Conformance | CI gating | Partial unit tests only | Partial | Partial | INT-441: flakes expected if network-based | Run conformance against local deterministic mock server. Add retries for the test runner itself only (not SDK). Add “flaky quarantine” process | Planned | Sahana Iyer | ENG-2485

---
TOP GAPS / PRIORITY (rough)
P0 (must fix for standardization release)
- TS: 429 retry aggressiveness + Retry-After compliance (SUP-9334)
- Streaming: no implicit reconnect; consistent cancel vs timeout; partial SSE frame parsing (support escalations)
- Timeouts: TS defaults (avoid infinite hangs); streaming inactivity timeout + clearer errors (SUP-9321)
- Auth: single env var + single header scheme; redaction; clearer missing-key message (SUP-9355)
- Go: consistent context cancel vs deadline (SUP-9342)

P1
- Error taxonomy + request-id attachment on all errors
- Telemetry hooks + safe logging helpers

Open questions / notes to resolve in review
- Do we allow opt-in long waits for Retry-After > 10s (or always fail fast)?
- Should streaming inactivity timeout be bytes-based or event-based? (proxy buffering vs silent models)
- Confirm gateway guarantees: request-id header name, Retry-After on 429/503, machine-readable rate limit fields.

Owners / next steps
- Ibrahim: turn this into spec outline + review checklist; drive ADR drafts for retries/streaming.
- Dana + Mateusz: inventory current streaming parsers and propose shared test vectors.
- Marcus: confirm Security stance on key sourcing + redaction requirements.
- Ethan/Amara: confirm gateway header + error payload guarantees needed by clients.

Change log
- 2025-01-13: Initial v1 matrix created (Ibrahim)
- 2025-01-15: Added support ticket references + preliminary P0 list (Dev Patel)
- 2025-01-17: Added conformance harness rows + retry budget proposal (Rafael + Sahana)
